Subject: SLO gating & multi-geo onramp — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier, Sarah + Evan — quick recap and the technical asks we discussed so your engineering team can validate feasibility for the pilot (called "onramp"). I tried to separate must-haves vs. wanted items so we can prioritize.

Quick summary of FinApps goals from today
- Targeting a live pilot in US + EU within 8 weeks. APAC considered a later phase.
- Primary workload: real-time document enrichment streams (clients send short prompts, expect streaming token responses to UI).
- Business SLOs drive infra: p95 generation latency for interactive UX, sustained throughput during morning peaks, and data residency for EU customers.

Must-haves (SLO gating for pilot acceptance)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency (request -> first token) <= 120 ms for US region; EU p95 <= 160 ms. APAC target left as aspirational (<= 220 ms) for phase 2.
- Streaming: support chunked token streaming with max inter-chunk gap of 30 ms for UI smoothness; resume on network hiccups without restarting conversation.
- Concurrency / throughput: support 100 concurrent interactive sessions per region with bursting to 300 for short windows (5–10 min).
- Persistence & KV cache: local per-region KV cache; cache hits should keep tail latency below 80 ms.
- Data residency: EU customer data (input + logs) must be stored and processed within EU region; no cross-border backups without GDPR-approved process.
- Auditability: basic request logs and redaction controls retained for 30 days; must be exportable to FinApps' SIEM.

Nice-to-haves (later phases or optional tuning)
- Auto-routing by geo affinity with fallback to nearby region when local capacity depleted.
- Quantization suggestions for cost reduction (we discussed 8-bit paths).

Attachments: I attached the high-level network diagram you sketched (finapps_network_arch.png) and our starter SLO matrix (redwood_slo_matrix.xlsx) with slots for FinApps' acceptance gates.

Next concrete actions
1) FinApps: Can you confirm the EU data residency requirement applies to both input payloads and generated text? (Sarah) — requested by Fri 8/21.
2) FinApps: Share a 24-hour traffic sample (timestamps, avg tokens per request, peak concurrent sessions) for our perf team to baseline — requested by Mon 8/24.
3) Redwood: Rishi to run a regional throughput simulation and validate burst profile; share preliminary numbers and any config knobs. — deliverable Wed 8/26.
4) Redwood: Priyom to draft a canary routing plan (geo affinity + fallback) and enumerate any tradeoffs on tail latency. — deliverable Thu 8/27.

If this all looks right I can kick off the internal perf simulation and loop in our infra SME for a short validation call.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — that aligns well. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) EU residency: yes, both POST payloads and generated outputs must remain in EU for EU-labeled accounts. We do allow anonymized aggregates to leave region for analytics, but only after a documented anonymization step.

2) Traffic sample: we'll pull a 24-hour sample from our prod proxy. Expect ~3–4 million tokens/day currently, with morning peak around 9–10am PST where concurrency spikes to ~220 for US. Each interactive session averages 150 tokens per request. We'll try to redact PII before sending.

3) Streaming tolerance: the UI team says inter-chunk gaps >50 ms are noticeable; 30 ms would be ideal but if you can guarantee <=50 ms worst-case that's acceptable for MVP.

We have a compliance follow-up: can Redwood provide a short statement on whether EU audit logs can be exported directly to a dedicated S3 bucket in the EU under our control? If so, what retention guarantees can you support?

I'll aim to answer Grace's confirmation question by end of day Friday.

Hi all — quick note from perf: we've started a baseline run against a representative 24-hour trace (synthetic replay) and an initial readout: 

- US (us-west-2-like test): p95 first-token latency = 112 ms with local KV cache hits (~60% hit rate). Under 100 concurrent sessions we see comfortable headroom; sustained 300 concurrent sessions raises p95 to ~210 ms without further sharding/batching changes.
- EU (eu-west-1-like test): p95 first-token ~150 ms with similar cache hit profile. We see additional network tail for some checkpoints near 180–200 ms under burst.
- Streaming inter-chunk gap: median 18 ms, 95th ~48 ms under our simulated network jitter.

Notes / implications:
- To meet FinApps' 120 ms p95 in US at sustained 220 concurrency, we'll likely want 2 dedicated serving shards with continuous batching tuned for short-context streaming and a larger KV cache footprint (increase from 16 GB to 48 GB per shard).
- For EU residency we can provision EU-local serving and log retention. Export to a FinApps-controlled S3 bucket in EU is supported via S3 connector; retention windows configurable (30/90/365 days) — we'll document policy and the data flow for compliance.

I can turn the synthetic test into a repeatable perf deck and include config knobs (shard count, cache size, batching window). Priyom and I will propose a default starter config for the pilot.

Actioning the plan: Rishi to share perf deck by Wed 8/26; Priyom to share routing/canary doc by Thu 8/27.

-rishi
